title: Grade 4 SOCIAL STUDIES — Premium Revision Paper #12

pages.quiz:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #12
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. On most maps, which direction is at the top? (1 mark)
   A. North
   B. South
   C. East
   D. West

2. Which direction is Mombasa from Nairobi on a map of Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. West
   B. North-west
   C. North
   D. South-east

3. Where does the sun rise? (1 mark)
   A. In the east
   B. In the south
   C. In the west
   D. In the north

4. What is the best way to compare the sizes of two counties on maps? (1 mark)
   A. Guess without a map
   B. Compare the length of the names
   C. Count the number of towns only
   D. Use the same scale and compare the areas

5. County X covers 8 grid squares and County Y covers 5 grid squares. Which statement is correct? (1 mark)
   A. They are the same size
   B. We cannot compare them
   C. County X is bigger than County Y
   D. County Y is bigger than County X

6. What is a mountain? (1 mark)
   A. Very high land with steep sides and a peak
   B. A large body of water
   C. A low place between hills
   D. A wide flat area

7. Which of these uses the water of a river to make electricity? (1 mark)
   A. A school
   B. A market
   C. A hydroelectric power station
   D. A church

8. Which physical feature helps people to catch fish? (1 mark)
   A. A lake
   B. A plateau
   C. A plain
   D. A hill

9. What is a lake? (1 mark)
   A. A dry plain
   B. A long channel of flowing water
   C. A large area of water surrounded by land
   D. A very high mountain

10. Which is the longest river inside Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Tana River
   B. Nzoia River
   C. Yala River
   D. Athi River

11. What is a season? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of clothing
   B. A type of crop
   C. The weather on one day
   D. A part of the year with a typical kind of weather

12. On a weather chart, which symbol usually means a sunny day? (1 mark)
   A. A wind arrow
   B. A cloud
   C. A sun
   D. A raindrop

13. Which monument in Nairobi remembers Kenya's independence in 1963? (1 mark)
   A. Thimlich Ohinga
   B. Fort Jesus
   C. Uhuru Gardens
   D. Lamu Fort

14. What is a cultural centre? (1 mark)
   A. A bank
   B. A place where the culture of communities is shown and kept alive
   C. A hospital
   D. A place for repairing cars

15. A tailor makes uniforms and a farmer buys them. What does the tailor need from the farmer? (1 mark)
   A. Cloth from the moon
   B. Nothing at all
   C. A tractor for sewing
   D. Food or money from selling food

16. Why must a key be included on a dot map? (1 mark)
   A. So that people know what each dot stands for
   B. So that colours are hidden
   C. So that it looks old
   D. So that the map is longer

17. In traditional culture, what do we call a basket or clay pot made and used by people? (1 mark)
   A. An artefact
   B. A river
   C. A kind of food
   D. A type of weather

18. Which game is played with seeds or stones moved between holes in a board? (1 mark)
   A. Netball
   B. Athletics
   C. Bao
   D. Football

19. Which of these is an artefact? (1 mark)
   A. A river
   B. A cloud
   C. A mountain
   D. A clay pot

20. Which is a traditional food eaten in many parts of Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Pizza
   B. Hamburger
   C. Ugali
   D. Sushi

21. Which words help to tell a history in order? (1 mark)
   A. First, then, later, today
   B. Up, down, left
   C. Red, blue, green
   D. Big, small, tall

22. Which is a good school rule? (1 mark)
   A. Write on walls
   B. Come to school on time
   C. Fight in class
   D. Break desks

23. What is a timeline? (1 mark)
   A. A picture of a school
   B. A kind of ruler
   C. A line showing events in the order they happened
   D. A weather chart

24. Keeping cattle, goats and camels in dry areas is called what? (1 mark)
   A. Mining
   B. Pastoralism
   C. Fishing
   D. Trading

25. Which national park in Narok County is famous for wildlife? (1 mark)
   A. Lake Victoria
   B. Kakamega
   C. Maasai Mara
   D. Nakuru town

26. Which activity earns money from visitors to game parks and beaches? (1 mark)
   A. Fishing
   B. Quarrying
   C. Mining
   D. Tourism

27. What is the raw material for tea? (1 mark)
   A. Tea leaves
   B. Sugarcane
   C. Cotton
   D. Fish

28. In Figure 3 of the lesson, the sugar factory employs 7 hundred workers. How many workers is that? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 7,000
   C. 700
   D. 70

29. Who keeps the money and records it in a school project? (1 mark)
   A. The treasurer
   B. The safety officer
   C. The gatekeeper
   D. The visitor

30. What is a budget? (1 mark)
   A. A crop
   B. A type of tool
   C. A plan of how much money you expect to spend and earn
   D. A game

31. Which is a good way to develop a quality like punctuality? (1 mark)
   A. Ignore it
   B. Wait for others to do it
   C. Practise it every day
   D. Practise it once a year

32. What does Stop-Think-Share teach? (1 mark)
   A. Share your password
   B. Ignore rules
   C. Think before you post
   D. Post quickly

33. Which of these can cause child abuse? (1 mark)
   A. Kind neighbours
   B. Enough food
   C. Poverty and harmful beliefs
   D. Good schools

34. Which of these can you call for help in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. A bakery
   B. The child helpline 116
   C. A cinema
   D. A shop

35. What does majority mean? (1 mark)
   A. No votes
   B. A tie
   C. The smaller number of votes
   D. The larger number of votes

36. Why is a Children's Government important? (1 mark)
   A. It stops learning
   B. It closes the school
   C. It punishes children
   D. It gives pupils a voice and shares responsibility

37. What is an agenda? (1 mark)
   A. A sports match
   B. A list of items to be discussed at a meeting
   C. A game
   D. A kind of food

38. What is the meaning of composition of a group? (1 mark)
   A. The song of the group
   B. The colour of the group
   C. The people or parts that make up the group
   D. The size of the room

39. Which of these is a way of participating in the Children's Government? (1 mark)
   A. Voting for leaders
   B. Breaking rules
   C. Laughing at leaders
   D. Ignoring elections

40. What are ECDE and pre-primary schools run by? (1 mark)
   A. Private banks only
   B. County governments
   C. Foreign governments
   D. The army

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Describe what people do in the cold season to stay healthy and warm. (4 marks)

42. State three road safety rules for a rainy day. (3 marks)

43. Name three kinds of community leaders. (3 marks)

44. Explain what interdependence means and give one example. (3 marks)

45. Give four instructions to guide a visitor from the school gate to the office using cardinal points. The office is 50 steps north and then 20 steps east of the gate. (4 marks)

46. List four democratic processes in a school. (4 marks)

47. Describe how you would prepare for a class visit to a museum, and what you would do during the visit. (5 marks)

48. Explain how a farmer and a trader depend on each other. (3 marks)

49. List four factors a company thinks about before building a factory. (4 marks)

50. Explain the meaning of an economic activity and give two examples. (3 marks)

51. Match each activity to a resource it uses: fishing, farming, mining, tourism. (4 marks)

52. Explain what peace means in a school. (2 marks)

53. A bar graph shows sub-county A has 40 thousand people and sub-county B has 25 thousand. Find the total population of the two sub-counties. (3 marks)

54. A dot map has 1 dot for every 1,000 people. A town has 12 dots and a dry area has 2 dots. How many more people live in the town? Show your working. (3 marks)

55. Explain why it is important to have a Children's Government in school. (4 marks)

56. Why should you never shelter under a tall tree during a thunderstorm? (2 marks)

57. Give three reasons why people need directions in everyday life. (3 marks)

58. Explain what may happen if people cut down all the trees on a mountain. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #12 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — North
   Maps are drawn with north at the top unless a north arrow shows otherwise.

2. D — South-east
   Mombasa lies to the south-east of Nairobi.

3. A — In the east
   The sun rises in the east and sets in the west.

4. D — Use the same scale and compare the areas
   To compare fairly we use maps drawn to the same scale.

5. C — County X is bigger than County Y
   8 squares is more land than 5 squares.

6. A — Very high land with steep sides and a peak
   A mountain is much higher than the land around it.

7. C — A hydroelectric power station
   Hydroelectric stations use falling river water to make electricity.

8. A — A lake
   People fish in lakes, rivers and the ocean.

9. C — A large area of water surrounded by land
   A lake has land all around it.

10. A — Tana River
   The Tana River is the longest river in Kenya.

11. D — A part of the year with a typical kind of weather
   A season is the weather that is typical over several months.

12. C — A sun
   A sun symbol shows sunny weather.

13. C — Uhuru Gardens
   Uhuru Gardens is where the Kenyan flag was first raised at independence.

14. B — A place where the culture of communities is shown and kept alive
   Cultural centres show dances, homes, crafts and foods.

15. D — Food or money from selling food
   The tailor depends on the farmer for food.

16. A — So that people know what each dot stands for
   Without a key we cannot read the dots.

17. A — An artefact
   Baskets and pots are artefacts.

18. C — Bao
   Bao is a board game with seeds.

19. D — A clay pot
   A clay pot is made by people.

20. C — Ugali
   Ugali is widely eaten in Kenya.

21. A — First, then, later, today
   Time words link events in order.

22. B — Come to school on time
   Being punctual is a good habit.

23. C — A line showing events in the order they happened
   A timeline shows events in order.

24. B — Pastoralism
   Pastoralism is keeping livestock on natural pasture.

25. C — Maasai Mara
   The Maasai Mara is in Narok County.

26. D — Tourism
   Tourism serves visitors.

27. A — Tea leaves
   Tea is made from tea leaves.

28. C — 700
   7 hundreds = 700.

29. A — The treasurer
   The treasurer handles and records money.

30. C — A plan of how much money you expect to spend and earn
   A budget plans money.

31. C — Practise it every day
   Habits grow with practice.

32. C — Think before you post
   We should think about whether it is true, kind and safe.

33. C — Poverty and harmful beliefs
   Poverty and harmful beliefs are causes.

34. B — The child helpline 116
   Childline Kenya can be reached on 116.

35. D — The larger number of votes
   Majority means more than others.

36. D — It gives pupils a voice and shares responsibility
   It teaches leadership and democracy.

37. B — A list of items to be discussed at a meeting
   An agenda gives the order of business.

38. C — The people or parts that make up the group
   Composition means the members that make up a group.

39. A — Voting for leaders
   Voting is part of participating.

40. B — County governments
   Pre-primary education is a county function.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: They wear warm clothes, eat and drink hot foods, sleep under blankets, and wash their hands to avoid colds and flu.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct action.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Do not cross flooded roads, wear bright or reflective clothes, and walk facing traffic if there is no pavement.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct rule.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Religious leaders, clan elders and village elders. Accept chiefs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each kind.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Interdependence means people depend on and help each other. For example, a farmer grows food and a trader sells it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for example, 1 mark for showing both sides need each other.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Start at the gate. Walk 50 steps north. Turn to face east. Walk 20 steps east to the office.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each clear instruction with the right direction.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Electing class monitors, class meetings, using a suggestion box, and voting on decisions.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each process.

47. (5 marks)
   Answer: Ask permission from the teacher and the museum, prepare questions, take a notebook, stay with the group, listen to the guide, take notes and do not touch objects.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct point, up to 5.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: The farmer grows crops and sells them to the trader. The trader carries the crops to town and sells them. The trader needs the crops and the farmer needs the buyer.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: Raw materials, market, transport, and water and power. Accept workers or land.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each factor.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: An economic activity is work done to earn income or produce goods and services. Examples are farming and fishing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for each example.

51. (4 marks)
   Answer: Fishing uses lakes or ocean, farming uses land and soil, mining uses minerals, tourism uses wildlife or beaches.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: Peace means pupils and teachers live together safely, respect each other and settle disagreements without fighting.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for safety and respect, 1 mark for solving conflict peacefully.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: 65 thousand, which is 65,000 people.
   Working / marking points: 40 + 25 = 65 thousand. 1 mark for adding, 1 mark for 65 thousand, 1 mark for 65,000.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: 10,000 more people.
   Working / marking points: 12 x 1,000 = 12,000; 2 x 1,000 = 2,000; 12,000 - 2,000 = 10,000. 1 mark for each step.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: It gives pupils a voice, teaches leadership, helps teachers with order and cleanliness, and teaches democracy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: Lightning can strike tall trees. It is safer to go into a strong building.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the danger, 1 mark for a safer choice.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: To find places, to travel safely, and to explain to others where something is. Accept sailors, pilots and farmers using direction.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible reason.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: Rain may wash away the soil. Rivers may dry up. There may be landslides or floods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct result.
